description: End-to-end live verifier ordering vectors (SPEC-v2 §2.5, §6, §7.2). Run the complete decision path with the given inputs and scripted Part B dependencies; compare the stage, error class or committed tuple, the exact receipt outbox body, and the number of times each callback ran. A committed outcome is not a released decision.

semantics.audience_memberships: caller-authenticated membership results returned by the audience provider
semantics.audience_mode: ok returns audience_memberships; error returns an error; panic panics
semantics.bundle: key into bundles_b64; the exact presented proof bundle bytes
semantics.callback_counts.evaluator: number of extension evaluator invocations; omitted when zero
semantics.callback_counts.progress: number of evaluation-progress writes to the claim store (SPEC-v2 §7.5): before trust resolution starts, after it completes, and after the status stage completes
semantics.callback_counts.status: number of status-provider invocations (one per issuer whose binding, anchoring and role checks passed)
semantics.claim_store: create = atomic claim succeeds with ClaimedAt = now + claim_time_offset; proof_conflict = challenge already claimed by a different proof digest; in_progress = exact retry while evaluating; terminal_replay = exact retry after commit; unavailable = store error. The claim store's finalization compare-and-set reads T_final = now + claim_time_offset + finalize_time_offset inside the compare-and-set: T_final < T_claim fails with clock_regressed, and an allow commits only while T_final < its allow horizon and T_final < the challenge expiry, else allow_horizon_passed; either failure commits nothing
semantics.configuration: now, max_challenge_age_seconds, future_skew_seconds, configured_replay_epoch (0..2^53-1), status_policy and status_keys are validated against the SPEC-v2 §2.5 bounds, together with the supplied request context (§5.2), after the bundle decodes (§6.2 step 2). The live verifier has one future skew: status_policy.clock_skew_seconds must equal future_skew_seconds, or the request is configuration_invalid. An expected_session_context_b64 that is not exactly 32 bytes is configuration_invalid at the same step
semantics.constraint_evaluators: caller-authenticated extension evaluator registry (SPEC-v2 §5.2); absent = none registered. Each entry's profile and type form the descriptor {"profile","type"} whose digest is sha384:hex(SHA-384("ratify-protocol-constraint-profile-v2" || 0x00 || RatifyCanonicalJSON(descriptor))). implementation binds the behavior: com.ratifyprotocol.max_count/v1 and com.ratifyprotocol.allowed_values/v1 are the standard profiles; fault:error returns an error; fault:panic panics; fault:timeout never answers within the registry timeout; fault:invalid_outcome returns an outcome outside pass/denied/unverifiable; fault:pass_until returns pass with horizon valid_until. The registry entries for types present in the chain are sealed with the claim and recorded, sorted by type, in the receipt member constraint_evaluators
semantics.journal: anchored = reference anchored store; absent = no store configured; unanchored = Load returns a head that does not match the record; load_error = Load fails; cas_conflict = every CompareAndSwap reports a conflict; cas_conflict_once = the 1st, 3rd, 5th, ... CompareAndSwap calls report a conflict and the others proceed. Setup: genesis, then ConfigureStatusKeyEpoch for every status_keys entry in ascending issuer_id order, then each preload object applied at its now under status_policy
semantics.rate: absent = no rate store; reserve = batch reserved; exceeded = definitive capacity exhaustion; unavailable = store error; panic = the store panics
semantics.receipt_body_b64: exact canonical receipt outbox body: every required receipt field except log_id, sequence, previous_receipt_hash and signature, plus agent_id
semantics.receiver_binding_hook: absent = no application hook; accept/reject = the pure application hook, invoked only after every built-in pre-claim check passed
semantics.request_context.extension_counts: authenticated named quantities for extension profiles: names 1 to 128 bytes of [a-z0-9_.:-], values 0..2^53-1, at most 64 entries; invalid is configuration_invalid before claim
semantics.request_context.extension_values: authenticated named exact values for extension profiles: names as for extension_counts, values valid UTF-8 of at most 512 bytes, at most 64 entries; invalid is configuration_invalid before claim
semantics.stage: preflight = rejected before claim (no receipt, nothing consumed); replay = claim already existed (no result disclosed, no evaluation); evaluating = claim created but nothing committed (error_class says why; lease-expiry recovery commits evaluation_interrupted later); committed = a terminal Protocol result was committed with receipt_body_b64 (not actionable until released)
semantics.status_evidence: per issuer_id provider response: mode ok returns objects (each object_type_code and exact wire bytes); error returns an error; panic panics. An issuer absent from the map returns an empty batch
semantics.status_keys: caller-authenticated status key per issuer_id (epoch and complete public key)
semantics.trust: null = provider returns unavailable; mode ok returns outcome (trusted with root_public_key, untrusted, unavailable, ambiguous); mode error returns an error; mode panic panics; mode registry = the SDK's reference candidate-record trust registry (SPEC-v2 §6.1) holding the complete public keys of registry in order: a record is a candidate when its key ID equals the chain's terminal issuer ID or either component equals the terminal issuer key's component; no candidate is untrusted, more than one (including the same key twice) is ambiguous and never a first match, exactly one is trusted with that record's key
semantics.tzdb_version: the configured IANA tzdata release required for time_window (SPEC-v2 §5.2); empty = not configured. The corpus assumes the pinned release named in SPEC-v2 §5.2; any other value makes every time_window constraint_unverifiable
semantics.verified_at: the authoritative claim time (T_claim) recorded in the receipt
